dynamically allocated array and read the values from keyboard in main. Display the result in the
main function.

questions.text:
Show the advantage of using pointers to swap two values when it is passed as a parameter to a
function.
questions.reason: Compare call-by-value with call-by-address to explain why swapping through pointers changes the caller's variables; this is conceptual explanation only.

questions.text:
Given the following sequence of letters and asterisks: EAS*Y*QUE***ST***IO*N***
Consider the queue data structure, supporting two operations insert and remove. Suppose that for
the above sequence, each letter (such as E) corresponds to an insert of that letter into the queue
and each asterisk (*) corresponds a remove operation on the queue. Show the sequence of values
returned by the remove operations.
questions.reason: Hand-simulate FIFO inserts and removes on the given sequence (the removes return E A S Y Q U E S T I O N); this is a pure trace.

questions.text:
Write a C program to accept a list of integer values from the user and insert them in a stack if they
are prime numbers. Display the final stack and handle all stack conditions properly.
questions.reason: Write a basic stack with push guarded by overflow/underflow checks, adding only values that pass a primality test, then display it. These are familiar single operations plus a simple filter.

questions.text:
Convert the given infix expression to prefix expression. Show the content of Stack at every step
A * (B + C / D) - E ^ F
questions.reason: Trace infix-to-prefix conversion with precedence and right-associative ^, showing the stack at each step. It is hand simulation; #150 covers evaluation, not conversion.

questions.text:
Write a C program to implement a doubly linked list that performs the following operations:
1 . Insert a node at the beginning of the list.
2 . Insert a node at the end of the list.

Display the list in forward and reverse order.
questions.reason: Implement DLL insertion at head and tail and print the list forwards and backwards. These are familiar single operations. #707 is partial: it covers addAtHead/addAtTail in a list that may be doubly linked, and it also includes index operations.

questions.text: Write a C program to delete the duplicate element from the linked list.
questions.reason: Remove duplicate values from a linked list (sorted order not stated, so use nested traversal or a lookup table) while unlinking and freeing nodes. This is standard pointer rewiring and the lower rating applies since no constraints are given. The catalog has no direct duplicate-removal list problem.

questions.text:
Implement a stack using a linked list in C with some Example. Write functions to perform stack
operations: push, pop, peek and isEmpty using liked list. Demonstrate these operations by pushing
multiple elements onto the stack, popping some elements, and displaying the stack's state after
each operation while handling stack underflow properly.
questions.reason: Implement push, pop, peek and isEmpty for a stack built from linked nodes, with underflow handling and a demonstration. These are familiar single operations; #155 adds a min requirement, so it is not a match.

questions.text:
Given the following Binary Search Tree with nodes inserted in order: 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80, 10,
25, 35, 45
Explain the cases of node deletion in a BST:

Deletion of a leaf node
Deletion of a node with one child
Deletion of a node with two children

Deletion of root node
questions.reason: Explain and illustrate the leaf, one-child, two-child and root deletion cases on a BST built from the given keys. The deliverable is explanation and tracing, not an implementation, so it is Easy.

questions.text:
Solve the following "A circular queue of size 6 initially contains elements [P, Q, R, S] with Front = 0
and Rear = 3. Perform the following operations: DEQUEUE(), ENQUEUE(T), ENQUEUE(U),
DEQUEUE(), ENQUEUE(V), ENQUEUE(W)
(I) Show the status of the queue after each operation.
(II) Indicate how Front and Rear pointers change after every operation.
(III) Explain how the wrap-around mechanism avoids unused spaces.
questions.reason: Trace the given dequeue/enqueue operations on a size-6 circular queue, recording Front and Rear (Rear wraps to 0 and then 1), and explain wraparound. This is a pure trace; #622 is the related implementation exercise.

questions.text:

1 . Adjacency Matrix
2 . Adjacency Lists
3 . Adjacency Multilists.
questions.reason: Describe adjacency matrix, adjacency list and adjacency multilist representations. This is definition and comparison only.

questions.text:
You are given the following sequence of letters and asterisks:
EAS*Y*QUE***ST***IO*N***
Each letter (such as E) represents an insert operation of that element into a data structure, and
each asterisk (*) represents a remove operation.

1 . Assume the data structure is a Stack (LIFO order). Show the sequence of elements that
would be removed (output sequence) during the remove operations.
2 . Assume the data structure is a Queue (FIFO order). Show the sequence of elements that
would be removed (output sequence) during the remove operations.
3 . Compare and explain briefly how and why the two output sequences differ, even though
the same sequence of operations is applied.
questions.reason: Hand-simulate a fixed insert/remove sequence on a stack and on a queue, then compare the LIFO and FIFO outputs. Queue is a secondary topic. This is a pure trace.

questions.text:
Write a C program that accepts integers continuously and inserts them into a stack until the user
enters a negative number. Display all elements in the stack.
questions.reason: Write a program that pushes integers until a negative number is entered and then displays the stack. Only basic push, an overflow check and traversal are needed.

questions.text:

A + B * (C ^ D - E) ^ (F + G * H) - I
questions.reason: Convert the given infix expression to prefix by hand, showing the stack at each step. The precedence and right-associative ^ handling make it longer but it is still a trace. #150 is postfix evaluation, not conversion.

questions.text:
Write the structure definition for a singly linked list node in C and function definitions to perform the
following operations:
i) Insert a new node at the end of the list
ii) Display the data of the middle node by traversing the list only once
iii) Display all node data in reverse order without actually reversing the list
questions.reason: Define the node structure and write three functions: insert at the end, find the middle node in one pass with slow/fast pointers, and print in reverse with recursion without changing the list. Each is a familiar standard operation. The catalog has no middle-node or reverse-print problem.

questions.text:
Write a C Program to do the following:
i) Create a circular singly linked list where each node contains an integer value.
ii) Insert a new node with a specified value after every node containing an even integer.
questions.reason: Build a circular singly linked list and insert a node after every even-valued node. The loop must stop correctly when it returns to the head and must skip the newly inserted nodes, which matters if the inserted value is itself even. These interacting conditions put it at the low end of Medium. The catalog has no circular-list match.

questions.text:
write a c program to implement stack using linked list and implement push() and pop() operation
with all necessary conditions
questions.reason: Implement a stack with linked nodes, including push and pop with an underflow check. This is a standard single-operation implementation. No direct catalog match.

Take the new element as input from the user
Insert the element in the correct position in the BST
Display the BST using inorder traversal after insertion

return whether the element is present or not.

questions.text:
A circular queue of size 6 is initially empty. Perform the following operations: ENQUEUE(10),
ENQUEUE(20), ENQUEUE(30), ENQUEUE(40), DEQUEUE(), ENQUEUE(50), ENQUEUE(60),
ENQUEUE(70), DEQUEUE(), ENQUEUE(80)

i) Show the contents of the queue after each operation.
ii) Track Front (F) and Rear (R) pointers after every step.
iii) Identify the step where overflow occurs and justify your answer.
questions.reason: Trace enqueue and dequeue on a circular queue of size 6, tracking front and rear and finding where overflow occurs. This is pure hand simulation. #622 covers the same circular-queue mechanics as an implementation task.

questions.text:
Given three sequences:
(i) 28, 16, 11, 19, 17, 25
(ii) 11, 16, 17, 19, 25, 28
(iii) 11, 17, 25, 19, 16, 28
Determine which one is preorder, inorder, and postorder sequences of the same binary tree, and
construct that tree.
questions.reason: Identify which sequence is which traversal: the sorted one is inorder, the one starting with root 28 is preorder, and the one ending with 28 is postorder. Then rebuild the tree. This is a hand construction using a standard method, and the catalog has no traversal-reconstruction problem.
